text:
Artemi Panarin has spent the last week and a half away from the Kings for family reasons, as Daily Faceoff reported, and missed Saturday's game too. His last game was November 12 against the Islanders.

When he plays, the Kings own the puck. He has 19 points in 17 games, and Los Angeles takes 61% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, nearly 16 points better than without him. Yet the Kings have scored 9.8 fewer goals than those chances deserve while he's out there, which has cost him points. That kind of bad luck usually swings back.

At 35, the undrafted former Calder winner is still a setup man first (Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 91st percentile for shot assists last season), and Evolving-Hockey ranked him 20th among all forwards. The Rangers traded him to Los Angeles last season; this is his first full year as a King. Our projection of about 86 points assumes he plays every remaining game, which depends on when he can return.
headline: Panarin's Kings line is better than his points
